question: The ban on selling new combustion engine vehicles from 20351 is one of the most harmful measures in the Green Deal. Far from fostering an orderly and realistic transition, this legislation threatens to destroy Europe’s productive fabric, and prompt industry relocations and massive job losses. Industry leaders are voicing their concerns. Mercedes-Benz CEO Ola Källenius has warned that Europe ‘needs a reality check.

Otherwise, we are heading full speed into a wall’2. According to BMW’s CEO, Oliver Zipse, the ban will hit the industry right at its ‘heart’, increasing reliance on China3, while Jean-Philippe Imparato (Stellantis) warns that, without a regulatory rethink before the end of the year, the company ‘will have to make tough decisions’4, hinting at possible factory closures in Europe. In view of the above: 1.
What is the expected timeline and scope of the revision of the 2035 zero-emission target?
Will the Commission assess the impact of this legislation on the EU’s productive fabric, especially in terms of employment, competitiveness and industrial sovereignty?
Before presenting any proposal to revise the target, will it publish a detailed roadmap and impact assessment that can be accessed by the public?

answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.10.2025) The Commission has accelerated work on the preparation of the foreseen review of the CO2 standards for cars and vans to come forward with the review by the end of 2025. On 7 July 2025, the Commission launched a Call for Evidence and a Public Consultation on the evaluation and review of this legislation1. The consultation has closed on 10 October 2025.

The Commission is currently conducting an impact assessment, after which the Commission will prepare a proposal for adoption under the ordinary legislative procedure. The impact assessment will explore a variety of options and compare them to the baseline. It will take into account technological developments and the importance of an economically viable and socially fair transition towards zero-emission mobility.
Once the impact assessment and the legislative proposal will be published, the public will again be provided with the opportunity to give feedback.
